item.title: alloca のような関数はどのようにスタックからメモリを割り当てるのでしょうか?
item.description:
📝 A little while ago, I talked about how compilers ensure that large stack allocations do not skip over the guard page. ” Yes, the _alloca() function calls the same _chkstk() function to probe the stack before adjusting the stack pointer for the allocated memory. h> void consume(void*,void*); void f(int n) { char buffer[16384]; consume(alloca(n), buffer); } On x86-64, this results in push rbp mov eax, 16416 ; probe for local frame call __chkstk sub rsp, rax ; create local frame lea rbp, [rsp+32] movsxd rax, ecx ; n lea rcx, [rax+15] ; round up to multiple of 16 and rcx, -16 mov rax, rcx ; special __chkstk calling convention call __chkstk sub rsp, rcx ; allocate n bytes lea rdx, [rbp] ; rdx -> buffer lea rcx, [rsp+32] ; rcx -> alloca'd memory call consume lea rsp, [rbp+16384] ; clean up local frame pop rbp ret 0 Observe that the same __chkstk function is used both for performing the initial stack probe when creating the local frame as well as for the alloca().
🔤 Original: How do functions like alloca allocate memory from the stack?
🔗 Read more: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20260817-40/?p=112617

item.title: 群衆カメラはアトランタの犯罪検挙率を改善していない
item.description:
